headline: Public hearing on a National Grid pole at Bridge and Flint streets, and $163,099 for High Street Park renovation.

Salem City Council Land Acknowledgement 
The Salem City Council honors that this land is Naumkeag, or fishing place, where 
generation of Naumkeag people from the Pawtucket band of the Massachusett Tribe lived 
and passed through for centuries. 
 
We acknowledge that this is unceded Indigenous land and also acknowledge the 
Massachusett Tribe, who continue to honor and hold this land into the present. 
 
Salem's City Council is committed to having ongoing meaningful dialogue with the 
indigenous peoples who have presence in Salem in order to dismantle the legacies of 
oppression and inequities that persist today.

Ordered: 
The Salem City Council hereby amends the 2023 Outdoor Dining Policy by deleting in its 
entirety the following section: 
“VII. Season. The outdoor dining season on public property extends from the first Friday in 
May through the first Monday in November. Licensees are responsible for removing and 
storing any outdoor dining equipment in the off-season. Applicants may request a waiver
9 
CITY OF SALEM 
November 12, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
from the City Council to keep their outdoor dining area open year-round, provided they take 
reasonable steps to prevent obstruction of snow removal.” 
and replacing it with the following: 
“Section VII. Season. The outdoor dining season on public property extends from the first 
Friday in May through the first Monday in November. Licensees are responsible for 
removing and storing any outdoor dining equipment in the off-season. Applicants may 
request a waiver to keep their outdoor dining area open year-round, provided they take 
reasonable steps to prevent obstruction of snow removal. Waiver applications should be 
made to the Licensing Department who shall review the request with relevant City 
departments and receive their approvals before forwarding the application with comment to 
the City Council for consideration. Any second and subsequent requests for waivers shall 
only be considered by the Licensing Department if the application is accompanied by 
documentation proving consistent sales and use of the outdoor dining area over the prior 
winter period when a waiver was granted. In the event of ice and/or snow, any sidewalk 
adjacent to the outdoor dining area must be kept free and clear of all snow and ice by the 
business. The City is not responsible for any damage to outdoor dining areas or associated 
furniture, furnishings, equipment, etc. due to City snow removal operations. Restaurants 
with approved winter waivers must keep outdoor seating areas and access to those areas, 
whether on the public way or private property, free and clear of snow and ice. A minimum 
clearance of 48” is required, while a clearance of at least 60” is preferred. The City 
reserves the right to reject future winter waiver applications from businesses that receive a 
winter waiver but do not utilize their outdoor dining area for consistent outdoor dining 
service over the winter season.”

RESOLUTION: To Support the Workers of the Peabody Essex Museum and Urge the 
Museum to Recognize their Desire to Form a Union
11 
CITY OF SALEM 
November 12, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 WHEREAS, As of November 1st, 2026, at least 66% of workers at the Peabody Essex 
Museum (a supermajority) have signed union authorization cards, indicating their intention 
to organize as part of the American Federation of Teachers; and 
WHEREAS, The Peabody Essex Museum is a highly respected, world-class institution in 
the city of Salem and its workers are crucial to its continued success; and 
WHEREAS, All workers in the City of Salem should be able to earn a living wage, find 
dignity and equity in their workplace, and enjoy the respect of their managers and 
employers; and 
WHEREAS, Many workers at other storied institutions around the Commonwealth have 
organized under labor unions, including the Museum of Fine Arts and, more recently, The 
Institute for Contemporary Art;  
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, The Salem City Council fully supports the 
unionization of workers at the Peabody Essex Museum; and 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, The Salem City Council is calling on management at the 
Peabody Essex Museum to voluntarily recognize the union and come to the bargaining 
table to begin an open dialogue between the museum and its workers.

An Ordinance to amend the Ordinance relative to Chapter 26, Parks and Recreation, 
relative to Charlotte Forten Park. 
Be it ordained by the City Council of the City of Salem, as follows: 
SECTION 1. Chapter 26, Parks and Recreation, is hereby amended by adding the 
following new Article V: 
“ARTICLE V. CHARLOTTE FORTEN PARK 
DIVISION 1. USE POLICY 
Sec. 26-130. Purpose and goals.
12 
CITY OF SALEM 
November 12, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
(a) Charlotte Forten Park (289 Derby Street, Salem) (“the park”) is for the use and 
enjoyment of the residents of the city and its visitors. Activities in the park should not 
interfere with or disturb the peace and enjoyment of all the residents of the city. 
(b) The goals of this policy are to: 
(1) Protect the park from adverse wear and tear. 
(2) Maintain handicapped accessibility. 
(3) Promote the following: 
a. Activities which are open to the public for public enjoyment. 
b. Passive recreation. 
c. Activities which develop public awareness and maintenance of the 
park. 
(c) No activities which will cause damage to the park will be allowed under any 
circumstance 
Sec. 26-131. Definitions. 
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the 
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates 
a different meaning: 
Disorderly conduct means any action intended to cause inconvenience, annoyance, 
or alarm, or which recklessly creates a risk thereof; fighting, threatening or violent 
behavior; wrestling in the vicinity of others; throwing breakable objects; throwing 
stones; or spitting. 
Harborwalk means the 10-foot-wide public walkway along the South River edge of 
the park. 
DIVISION 2. PROHIBITED ACTIVITIES; PENALTIES AND ENFORCEMENT 
Sec. 26-132. Prohibited activities. 
The following activities are strictly prohibited in Charlotte Forten Park: 
(1) Destruction, defacement, removal, or disturbance of any sign, equipment, 
monument, marker, planting, or structure.
13 
CITY OF SALEM 
November 12, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
(2) Distribution or display of commercial advertising, soliciting of business, or 
any other commercial transactions, except in connection with an event 
permitted by the city. 
(3) Selling, keeping or offering or exposing for sale, any goods, wares, 
merchandise, or services, except in connection with an event permitted by the 
city. 
(4) Operation of devices in violation of Chapter 22, Noise Ordinance. 
(5) Disorderly conduct. 
(6) Use of metal-detecting devices. 
(7) Non-permitted vehicles. 
(8) Digging or disturbing the soil. 
(9) Drinking alcoholic beverages, except in connection with an event 
permitted by the city. 
(10) Climbing on trees and fences. 
(11) Using grills or making fires, except in connection with an event permitted 
by the city. 
(12) Entering between sunset and sunrise, except on the Harborwalk, in 
connection with an event permitted by the city, or if an employee or contractor 
for the City of Salem engaged in work on behalf of the City of Salem. 
(13) Leaving trash, waste, or refuse, which may, at the discretion of police, 
public services, or health department officials, be removed immediately. 
(14) Carrying or having in one's possession a lighted cigarette, cigar or pipe, 
or other object used for a similar purpose, giving off or containing any 
substance giving off smoke. 
(15) Setting up tables, tents, displays, or other objects or obstructions, except 
in connection with an event permitted by the city. 
Nothing in this article shall be construed to limit any rights under a recorded 
easement. 
Sec. 26-133. Penalties and enforcement.
14 
CITY OF SALEM 
November 12, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
Whoever violates any provision of this article shall be subject to a fine of $150 for 
the first offense, $200 for a second offense, and $300 for a third and subsequent 
offense. The police and health department officials shall enforce this division.” 
SECTION 2. 
This ordinance shall take effect as provided by City Charter.

COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS, EXECUTIVE OFFICE OF ENERGY AND 
ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS FOR THE PARC GRANT PROGRAM FOR THE
15 
CITY OF SALEM

RENOVATION OF HIGH STREET PARK. 
 
Whereas: High Street Park is a community-wide asset. Preservation and 
improvements to this Park are a City priority as evidenced in the most recent Open 
Space and Recreation Plan; and 
Whereas: The High Street Park Renovation Project will greatly enhance this Park by 
upgrading the play structures, vegetation, and recreation amenities; and 
Whereas: Overall cost and fiscal budget constraints prevented the City from 
proceeding forward with project implementation; and 
Whereas: The project was viewed as feasible only when fiscal resources were 
available, with the intention of securing grant funding, when and if available, to assist 
in this effort; and 
Whereas: The Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs (EEA) is 
offering reimbursable grants to cities and towns to support the preservation and 
restoration of parks through the Parkland Acquisitions and Renovations for 
Communities (PARC) Grant Program (formerly Urban Self-Help Act) 301 CMR 5.00; 
and 
Whereas: The project will cost a total of $1,246,576. 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT 
1. That the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to file and accept grants from the 
Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs; and 
2. That the Council hereby authorizes $1,246,576 to implement the project, sourced 
from Capital Improvement Program (CIP), Community Preservation Act (CPA), and 
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), to be reimbursed up to a maximum 
amount of $425,000 by the EEA; and 
3. That the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to take such other actions as are necessary 
to carry out the terms,                
purposes, and conditions of this grant to be administered by the Department of Planning 
and Community Development; and 
 
4. That High Street Park is a dedicated park under M.G.L. Chapter 45, Section 3; 
and

awarding of said PARC Grant and be null and void in the event no grant is awarded.

An Ordinance to amend an Ordinance relative to Chapter 24, Section 33, Outdoor Lighting 
Be it ordained by the City Council of the City of Salem, as follows: 
Chapter 24, Section 33, Outdoor Lighting  
Section I: Regulations 
No outdoor floodlighting or decorative lighting, except lighting primarily 
designed to illuminate walks, driveways, parking areas, outdoor living areas, 
or outdoor recreational facilities, emergency lighting associated an alarm or 
other life or building safety system, or temporary holiday lighting in use for not 
longer than an eight-week period in any calendar year, shall be allowed. Any 
permanent lighting allowed pursuant to this section shall be continuous, 
indirect, and installed in a manner that will prevent direct light from shining 
onto any abutting property. All municipal and public school lighting shall be 
exempt from the provisions of this ordinance.  
Section II: Enforcement and appeals 
The Building Inspector, or their designee, shall enforce this division. Appeals 
of any violations of this section shall be made to the Municipal Hearing 
Officer. 
Section III: Penalties 
Whoever violates any provision of this section shall be subject to a fine of $50.00 
for the first offense, $150.00 for the second offense, and $300.00 for the third and 
subsequent offenses. 
Section IV: This Ordinance shall take effect as provided by City Charter.
